<atomic>A Boy Scout lantern.</atomic>
<atomic>Professionally built structure.</atomic>
<atomic>The gang's got sleeping bags.</atomic>
<atomic>They're roasting marshmallows over a Cub Scout camping stove.</atomic>
<atomic>Ham's brought personal s'mores supplies.</atomic>

<atomic>Wanna s'more?</atomic>

contents.text: INT. TREE HOUSE - NIGHT
A Boy Scout lantern. Professionally built structure. The gang's got sleeping bags. They're roasting marshmallows over a Cub Scout camping stove. Ham's brought personal s'mores supplies.
HAM: Wanna s'more?
SCOTTY: Some more of what?
HAM: No. You wanna s'more?
SCOTTY: I haven't had anything yet, so how can I have any more of nothing?
HAM: You're killing me, Smalls. Look, these are s'mores stuff. Pay attention.

contents.text: Dr. King compares justice to water and righteousness to "a mighty stream" in order to give his speech an urgent tone.

contents.text: By comparing Juliet to the sun, Shakespeare shows how Romeo idealizes Juliet.

<atomic>You've waited too long.</atomic>

contents.text: I know where I have to go. I've known for a long time. I made a promise. The kind of promise you don't break because, if you break it, you've broken part of yourself, maybe the most important part.

But you tell yourself things. Things like, I need to come up with something first. I can't just walk into the lion's den without a plan. Or, It's hopeless, there's no point anymore. You've waited too long.
<citation>From Rick Yancey, The 5th Wave. Copyright 2013 by Rick Yancey</citation>

text.text: <atomic>The desire to express myself grew.</atomic>
<atomic>The few signs I used became less and less adequate,</atomic>
<atomic>and my failures to make myself understood were always followed by outbursts of passion.</atomic>

text.text: <atomic>On a melancholy day in autumn, when the shadows of morning and evening throw a gloom over the decline of the year, I passed several hours in rambling about Westminster Abbey. As I passed its threshold, it seemed like stepping back in time and losing myself among the shades of former ages.</atomic>

<atomic>Bright sunshine fell upon the old red sandstone of which the later part of the old Abbey Farmery is built, and cast a glare on the snow-covered roof. The day was deliciously crisp, clear, and invigorating, and Bess laughed and snowballed me and the dogs, and so we wandered away inside.</atomic>

text.text: <atomic>The lower part of the castle was hollowed into cloisters. An awful silence reigned throughout those subterraneous regions, except now and then some blasts of wind that shook the doors she had passed, and which, grating on the rusty hinges, were re-echoed through that labyrinth of darkness. Every murmur struck her with new terror.</atomic>

<atomic>Before him, Belpher Castle towered against a light blue sky. On either side, rolling park land spread as far as the eye could see, carpeted here and there with violets, dotted with great oaks and ashes and Spanish chestnuts, orderly, peaceful, and English. Somewhere in the distance sounded the tinkle of sheep bells.</atomic>

<atomic>Then there was the peculiar dying reference to a rat. What could that mean? It could not be delirium. A man dying from a sudden blow does not commonly become delirious. No, it was more likely to be an attempt to explain how he met his fate. But what could it indicate?</atomic>

<atomic>Then there was the peculiar dying reference to a rat. What could that mean? It could not be delirium. A man dying from a sudden blow does not commonly become delirious. No, it was more likely to be an attempt to explain how he met his fate. But what could it indicate?</atomic>

The other passage uses words like alarming, suspense, fearful, and trembling to convey an anxious tone.
Select the passage that has a more concerned tone.

<atomic>I gasped for breath—and yet the officers heard it not. Why would they not be gone? I paced the floor to and fro with heavy strides, as if excited to fury by the observations of the men—but the noise steadily increased. Oh, God! What could I do?</atomic>

text.text: <atomic>On a melancholy day in autumn, when the shadows of morning and evening throw a gloom over the decline of the year, I passed several hours in rambling about Westminster Abbey. As I passed its threshold, it seemed like stepping back in time and losing myself among the shades of former ages.</atomic>

<atomic>Bright sunshine fell upon the old red sandstone of which the later part of the old Abbey Farmery is built, and cast a glare on the snow-covered roof. The day was deliciously crisp, clear, and invigorating, and Bess laughed and snowballed me and the dogs, and so we wandered away inside.</atomic>

text.text: <atomic>On a melancholy day in autumn, when the shadows of morning and evening throw a gloom over the decline of the year, I passed several hours in rambling about Westminster Abbey. <atomic>Rose sat all alone in the big best parlor, with her little handkerchief ready to catch the first tear, for she was thinking of her troubles. She had retired to this room as a good place in which to be miserable; for it was dark and still, full of ancient furniture and somber curtains.</atomic>

content.text: Tone

pieces.text: is the

content.text: attitude

pieces.text: that is expressed in a text. A writer's tone can communicate a range of feelings, such as excitement, humor, doubt, or respect.

contents.text: Tone is revealed through the language that a writer uses in a text. For example, is the information presented through direct statements or through figurative language? Is the topic described through positive words and phrases or through negative ones? These types of text features can help express different tones.

elements.text: I shivered as I watched the bitter wind whip through the gray, sickly trees outside.

content.text: Words like "bitter," "gray," and "sickly" create a mournful, depressed tone.

elements.text: With a triumphant fist in the air, the runner dashed across the finish line to victory.

content.text: Words like "triumphant," "dashed," and "victory" create an upbeat, energetic tone.

The first passage is more delighted in tone. It uses words and phrases like charmed, warmed her heart, and appreciated to show a pleased and joyous tone. The other passage uses words and phrases like thinking of her troubles, good place in which to be miserable, and dark and still to convey a mournful attitude.

<atomic>If anything, it was all too easy and over too fast.</atomic>
<atomic>When he was done, he unwound his safety line and gave a hand signal to Dex's first mate, Joe Kahali, down below.</atomic>
<atomic>Joe put both hands on the winch at the base of the mast and started cranking Carter back down the deck.</atomic>

header.text: <instructions>Select the best evidence to support the statement that the narrator's house doesn't have running water.</instructions>

text.text: <atomic>My house stood silently peeking back at me through the trees, a square box painted dark green.…It was the only home I'd ever known, and I loved it.</atomic>
<atomic>I loved its silver-painted corrugated iron roof, which slanted down into gutters that flowed into the round water tank in the back. It made nice sounds in the rain.</atomic>
<atomic>The only water we had was what we caught off the roof. Not like Billy's house, where they had water pipes from the street, and a bathroom inside the house.</atomic>
<atomic>"Hey," Billy whispered, quickly moving off the trail into the trees. His blond hair glowed where the sun hit it, but mostly he was in the shade.</atomic>

<atomic>Jess slid out of bed and into his overalls.</atomic>
<atomic>He didn't worry about a shirt because once he began running he would be hot as popping grease even if the morning air was chill,</atomic>
<atomic>or shoes because the bottoms of his feet were by now as tough as his worn-out sneakers.</atomic>

text.text: <atomic>My house stood silently peeking back at me through the trees, a square box painted dark green.…It was the only home I'd ever known, and I loved it.</atomic>
<atomic>I loved its silver-painted corrugated iron roof, which slanted down into gutters that flowed into the round water tank in the back. It made nice sounds in the rain.</atomic>
<atomic>The only water we had was what we caught off the roof. Not like Billy's house, where they had water pipes from the street, and a bathroom inside the house.</atomic>
<atomic>"Hey," Billy whispered, quickly moving off the trail into the trees. His blond hair glowed where the sun hit it, but mostly he was in the shade.</atomic>

contents.text: Denotation is the literal meaning of a word that can be found in a dictionary.
Connotation is the feeling or idea that goes along with a word.

Many words with similar denotations have different connotations. For example, think about the words frugal and miserly. Both denote tending to save money, but frugal has a more positive connotation and suggests a person is careful with money, while miserly has a more negative connotation and suggests a person is cheap or stingy.

To make appropriate word choices, you must consider more than just a word's denotation. Choosing a word with a different connotation can convey the same kind of information while creating a different mood or tone.
